record.paper_title: The True Prosoluble Completion of a Group: Examples and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Free versus nonfree true prosoluble completions
record.original_question: Does there exist a finitely generated free group F, a residually soluble group Gamma that is not free, and a homomorphism psi: F -> Gamma such that for every j >= 1 the induced homomorphism F/D_j(F) -> Gamma/D_j(Gamma) is an isomorphism, where D_j denotes the j-th term of the ordinary derived series? Equivalently, does there exist such F, Gamma, and psi for which the induced map on true prosoluble completions PS(psi): PS(F) -> PS(Gamma) is an isomorphism?

evidence.quote: We do not know if there exist a finitely generated free group F, a group Γ which is residually soluble and not free, and a homomorphism ψ : F −→ Γ such that ψ induces an isomorphism F/Dj (F ) −→ Γ/Dj (Γ) for all j ≥ 1, or equivalently such that P S(ψ) : P S(F ) −→ P S(Γ) is an isomorphism.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a group G, let D_1(G)=G and D_{j+1}(G)=[D_j(G),D_j(G)] denote the j-th term of the ordinary derived series. A group G is residually soluble if the intersection of all D_j(G), j≥1, is trivial. The true prosoluble completion of G is the inverse limit PS(G) = lim G/N taken over all normal subgroups N⊴G such that G/N is a (possibly infinite) soluble group; equivalently, when G is residually soluble, PS(G) can be described as the inverse limit of the system {G/D_j(G)}_{j≥1} together with all soluble quotients refining it.

Question: Do there exist a finitely generated free group F, a finitely generated residually soluble group Γ that is not free, and a homomorphism ψ: F → Γ such that for every j ≥ 1 the induced homomorphism F/D_j(F) → Γ/D_j(Γ) is an isomorphism? Equivalently, do there exist such F, Γ, ψ for which the induced map PS(ψ): PS(F) → PS(Γ) on true prosoluble completions is an isomorphism?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work of Jaikin-Zapirain on the finite and solvable genus of finitely generated free and surface groups establishes a Grothendieck-rigidity result for free groups in the soluble setting: if F is a finitely generated free group, G is a finitely generated residually (finite) soluble group, and u: F → G induces an isomorphism on pro-(finite soluble) completions, then u is itself an isomorphism, so G is free. Since the hypothesis F/D_j(F) ≅ Γ/D_j(Γ) for all j (equivalently, PS(ψ) is an isomorphism) implies the pro-(finite soluble) completion is an isomorphism, this rules out any non-free Γ as in the question. The answer is therefore negative.

status_evidence.title: The finite and solvable genus of finitely generated free and surface groups
status_evidence.snippet: If F is a free group and G is a finitely generated residually-C group with a homomorphism u: F → G such that the induced map of pro-C completions is an isomorphism, then u is an isomorphism.
status_evidence.claim: Jaikin-Zapirain proves a Grothendieck-rigidity statement for free groups with respect to the pro-(finite soluble) completion, implying that any Γ as in the question must be free.

status_evidence.title: The finite and solvable genus of finitely generated free and surface groups (preprint)
status_evidence.snippet: Solvable genus of a finitely generated free group; groups with the same finite soluble quotients as a free group are themselves free under the stated rigidity result.
status_evidence.claim: The solvable genus result yields that a finitely generated residually soluble group sharing all soluble quotients with a free group via a homomorphism must be free.
